title: Terence Tao Reposts Boycott Statement: Mathematics Community Fully Cuts Ties With OpenAI
key_facts: The Human Mathematics Association issued a statement urging mathematicians to stop cooperating with OpenAI after OpenAI's release of more than 700 math manuscripts at once.

The association says mathematicians 'did not ask for this work to be done' and calls the release a display of power; members commit not to work for commercial AI companies or publish AI-generated maths texts.
36Kr says Terence Tao, a Fields Medal winner, reposted the statement on his personal blog, but he does not appear in the association's member list.
The association was founded in August 2026 and has 809 members, most of them graduate students, per netizens cited by 36Kr; a separate declaration was signed by 28 Fields Medal winners.
Critics say only 162 of the 722 papers had main results checked by computer; OpenAI withdrew 3 manuscripts the next day, revised 14 and updated citations in 13.
OpenAI's GitHub README says some unformalized results may have problems and it will fix them.
Supporters of OpenAI cite early independent Lean re-checks of some results that passed.
quote_evidence: This is a special statement released by the Human Mathematics Association in response to OpenAI's massive release of mathematical research results.
Terence Tao, a Chinese mathematician and Fields Medal winner, reposted this statement on his personal blog.

The next day after the release, OpenAI also removed 3 manuscripts: a symbol error invalidated a core argument, which in turn affected two papers that relied on it; another 14 papers were revised, and 13 papers had their citation relationships updated.
why_it_matters_hint: A small group is turning the dispute over AI-produced proofs into a call for a boycott, while the proofs' reliability is still being checked.
event_date: Statement reported 9 Oct 2026; OpenAI's release was in early October 2026
notes: 36Kr piece mixes reporting with opinion; only attributed facts used. The headline 'Mathematics Community Fully Cuts Ties' overstates: the group has about 800 members. Our 9 Oct 2026 edition carried The Decoder's report of the boycott call (pool 1009:C04-01); the OpenAI release was covered 6 Oct (The Verge, NYT).
